hints: Remember that every single bond is one sigma bond, while a double bond counts as one sigma plus one pi.
Start by sketching ethene, $\text{C}_2\text{H}_4$, and count 4 C-H sigmas plus 1 C-C sigma for a total of 5.
Now count carefully for ethanol, ethanal and ethanoic acid, then check which totals are odd numbers to find how many qualify.
walkthrough:
**Recall the sigma counting rule**

Every single bond contains exactly one $\sigma$ bond. A double bond contains one $\sigma$ and one $\pi$ bond, so it still only contributes one to the $\sigma$ count.

Rule:
$$\text{single bond = 1 } \sigma, \quad \text{double bond = 1 } \sigma + 1 \pi$$

**Count for ethene and ethanol**

Draw $\text{CH}_2=\text{CH}_2$. There are 4 C-H singles and 1 C=C sigma. Total = 5, which is odd.

Draw $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{OH}$. There are 5 C-H + 1 C-C + 1 C-O + 1 O-H = 8 $\sigma$ bonds, which is even.

**Count for ethanal and ethanoic acid**

Draw $\text{CH}_3\text{CHO}$. There are 4 C-H + 1 C-C + 1 C=O sigma = 6 $\sigma$ bonds, which is even.

Draw $\text{CH}_3\text{CO}_2\text{H}$. There are 3 C-H + 1 C-C + 1 C=O sigma + 1 C-O + 1 O-H = 7 $\sigma$ bonds, which is odd.

**Decide how many are odd**

Odd $\sigma$ counts are $\text{C}_2\text{H}_4$ (5) and $\text{CH}_3\text{CO}_2\text{H}$ (7). That is 2 compounds in total.

options.A: 1 is too low. You get this if you spot only ethene with 5 sigma bonds but miscount ethanoic acid, often by forgetting the O-H sigma or by counting the C=O as two sigmas.
options.B: 2 is correct. $\text{C}_2\text{H}_4$ has 5 sigma bonds and $\text{CH}_3\text{CO}_2\text{H}$ has 7 sigma bonds, both odd. $\text{C}_2\text{H}_5\text{OH}$ has 8 and $\text{CH}_3\text{CHO}$ has 6, both even.
options.C: 3 is incorrect. You get this if you miscount ethanol as 9 or ethanal as 7, usually by counting a pi bond as a sigma bond or by adding an extra H.
options.D: 4 is incorrect. This assumes all four are odd, which happens if you count every bond in a double bond as sigma, so you add one extra sigma for each C=C or C=O.
